snippet.title: 3 breakout stocks to watch for tomorrow?
snippet.description:
3 breakout stocks near all-time highs on the daily chart — with clear risk-reward signals, not just momentum. First up is HFCL, which has recovered ~20% after correcting from its previous all-time high and is attempting another breakout; a close above 230 confirms the setup, while a close below 222 invalidates it. Next is Pidilite Industries, showing renewed strength after ~2 years of consolidation — the breakout confirms on a close above 1,692, and the trend invalidates below 1,653. Finally, Endurance Technologies has traded below its previous all-time high for about a year and is now back at the breakout zone; a closing break above 3,050 confirms, below 2,980 it's invalid. Remember: fresh momentum signals still need stop-loss protection for downside. Prices as of August 13, 2026. Which other breakout stocks are you tracking? Drop them in the comments.

snippet.description:

In this video, we break down what drove the latest numbers, the opportunity ahead, and the key risk investors should watch.

snippet.title: Sunil Singhania’s Fund is Buying this Stock after a 50% Fall?
snippet.description:
Sunil Singhania's Abakkus fund is quietly accumulating a stake in Mrs Bectors Food Specialities, a stock still down 50% from its highs — and the latest Q1FY27 concall hints at a turnaround. This fundamental analysis breaks down why the stock fell (100x peak PE, slowing growth, shrinking margins through FY25-FY26), and why the story may be changing now: QSR-led institutional sales delivering double-digit growth, exports (35% of revenue) growing despite higher freight costs, and the bakery division emerging as the company's real strategic growth engine with EBITDA margins guided from 13% today to 14% in FY27 and 15-16% by FY30, backed by a planned ₹200 crore capex. We also cover the risk that could delay the comeback — rising input costs across raw material, packaging, fuel and logistics — and why management expects recovery only from Q3FY27. If you track smallcap turnaround stocks, institutional buying activity, and quarterly earnings triggers in the Indian stock market, this fundamental and technical breakdown of Mrs Bectors Food Specialities Ltd is for you. snippet.title: Market Timing vs Staying Invested: 19 Years of Data
snippet.description:
Can trying to be smarter with your mutual fund investments actually hurt your returns?

Using nearly two decades of market data, we tested three common strategies—lump sum vs SIP, profit booking, and investing more during market crashes. The results challenge some popular investing assumptions and show why waiting for the perfect opportunity may not always work in your favour. The key takeaway: investing earlier, staying invested longer, and remaining disciplined can be more powerful than trying to time the market.

snippet.title: Why Does Nifty Jump After 3:30? New CAS Closing Rules Explained
snippet.description:
NSE's new Closing Auction Session (CAS) is changing how F&O-eligible stocks get their closing price — and if you trade Nifty futures and options, this directly affects your expiry-day risk. In this video, we break down exactly how the closing auction session works: normal trading for CAS-eligible stocks stops at 315, the reference price is set using the 3 to 315 VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price), and the auction runs in phases until final order-entry closure between 328-330 — while Nifty futures and options keep trading until 340. We explain why this creates a settlement risk window for F&O traders on expiry days, how a large order in a heavyweight stock can move the auction price and Nifty's final close, why the Nifty chart can show a sudden large candle after 315, and what this means for your options' intrinsic value, square-off timing, and hedging strategy. Whether you're new to intraday trading or actively trading in the stock market, understanding this closing auction mechanism is now essential to avoid getting caught off guard on expiry day. Disclaimer: This video is for educational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. Please consult your financial advisor before making any investment decisions. #Groww #CAS #stockmarket

1:17 - CAS impact on F&O traders

snippet.title: This indicator predicts gold market cycles most of the time?
snippet.description:

Before you check the chart, look at a hidden indicator that has predicted every major gold move for the last 26 years — the US Bond Yield Spread (10-year minus 2-year Treasury yield). In this video, we break down how to plot the US yield spread against the gold price on TradingView and show a 26-year, period-by-period backtest — 2001-2003, 2004-2005, 2006, 2011-2013, 2013-2016, 2019-2021, 2021-2023, and 2023-2026 — comparing yield spread direction to actual gold returns, including the sharp correction happening in gold right now in 2026. This is a data-backed pattern breakdown for gold price prediction and gold investment in India, not a buy/sell recommendation — always do your own research before making any investment decision. Watch till the end to learn how to track this indicator yourself, and drop in the comments what percentage of your portfolio is currently allocated to gold.

localized.title: This indicator predicts gold market cycles most of the time?
localized.description:
Is gold about to go up or down? Before you check the chart, look at a hidden indicator that has predicted every major gold move for the last 26 years — the US Bond Yield Spread (10-year minus 2-year Treasury yield). In this video, we break down how to plot the US yield spread against the gold price on TradingView and show a 26-year, period-by-period backtest — 2001-2003, 2004-2005, 2006, 2011-2013, 2013-2016, 2019-2021, 2021-2023, and 2023-2026 — comparing yield spread direction to actual gold returns, including the sharp correction happening in gold right now in 2026. This is a data-backed pattern breakdown for gold price prediction and gold investment in India, not a buy/sell recommendation — always do your own research before making any investment decision. Watch till the end to learn how to track this indicator yourself, and drop in the comments what percentage of your portfolio is currently allocated to gold.

snippet.title: Stock Market Closing Rules Changed | SEBI CAS Impact on Intraday & F&O Traders Explained
snippet.description:
From 3 August 2026, the Indian stock market is introducing major changes to its market closing process that every trader and investor should know. In this video, we explain the new Closing Auction Session (CAS) introduced by SEBI, how the closing price of 200+ F&O-enabled stocks will now be determined, why the traditional 30-minute VWAP method is being replaced, and how extended F&O trading hours until 3:40 PM will impact stock futures, options, delivery, intraday, and MTF traders. We also break down the complete CAS timeline, reference price, equilibrium price calculation, order restrictions, auto square-off timing changes, and the impact on mutual fund NAVs, derivative settlement, portfolio valuation, and collateral value. If you trade in the Indian stock market, especially in F&O-enabled stocks, this market update will help you stay prepared for the new SEBI rules effective from 3 August 2026. (Source: SEBI Circular)

snippet.title: 5 Growth Stocks at Make-or-Break Levels
snippet.description:
Many investors feel safer buying a stock that has fallen sharply, because it looks “cheap.” But a falling stock is not always undervalued, and a stock trading near its 52-week high is not always expensive.

In this video, we explain why 52-week highs can sometimes signal strong momentum, improving fundamentals, better business performance, or institutional interest. We also look at why blindly buying fallen stocks can be risky if the market is pricing in real problems like weak growth, rising debt, poor cash flows, or governance concerns.

Watch this video to understand when price strength can be a positive signal — and why fundamentals and valuation still matter.

snippet.title: Buying Stocks at 52-Week High Is Not a Bad Idea!
snippet.description:
Many investors feel safer buying a stock that has fallen sharply, because it looks “cheap.” But a falling stock is not always undervalued, and a stock trading near its 52-week high is not always expensive.

In this video, we explain why 52-week highs can sometimes signal strong momentum, improving fundamentals, better business performance, or institutional interest. We also look at why blindly buying fallen stocks can be risky if the market is pricing in real problems like weak growth, rising debt, poor cash flows, or governance concerns.

Watch this video to understand when price strength can be a positive signal, and why fundamentals and valuation still matter.

snippet.title: This Company Certifies Diamonds for Profit with 60% margins?
snippet.description:
International Gemological Institute (IGI) operates a high-margin diamond certification business, testing and grading natural diamonds, lab-grown diamonds, jewellery and gemstones. With nearly 65% share in the global lab-grown diamond certification market, around 50% certification volume share in India and close to 60% EBITDA margins, IGI has built a strong market position. However, revenue growth slowed to 16% in CY25, compared with much higher growth before its December 2024 listing. This video analyses IGI’s business model, market share, financial performance, FY27 growth guidance, valuation correction and key risks, including slowing jewellery demand and weaker certification volumes.

localized.title: This Company Certifies Diamonds for Profit with 60% margins?
localized.description:
International Gemological Institute (IGI) operates a high-margin diamond certification business, testing and grading natural diamonds, lab-grown diamonds, jewellery and gemstones. However, revenue growth slowed to 16% in CY25, compared with much higher growth before its December 2024 listing. This video analyses IGI’s business model, market share, financial performance, FY27 growth guidance, valuation correction and key risks, including slowing jewellery demand and weaker certification volumes.

snippet.title: Why HDFC and Axis Bank Stock Fell After Q1 Results?
snippet.description:
HDFC Bank reported a quarterly profit of ₹19,060 crore, yet its stock fell nearly 5% in a single day. The key concern was not the headline profit but the quality of earnings. Lower provisions supported profits, while core lending profitability remained under pressure as Net Interest Margin declined to 3.26%. Despite nearly 15% loan growth, Net Interest Income increased by only around 7%, lagging major peers such as ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank. This video explains why investors reacted negatively, what the loan growth–earnings disconnect means, and whether the margin pressure is temporary or signals a longer-term challenge for HDFC Bank.

snippet.title: Quality Stocks at Cheap Valuation: Charlie Munger’s 200-WMA Strategy?
snippet.description:
Discover Charlie Munger’s disciplined investing approach by utilizing the 200-week moving average (200-WMA) to identify quality stocks at attractive valuations. This strategy helps investors look past short-term market hype, pinpointing opportunities when high-quality businesses consolidate near their long-term average price zones. Learn how to maintain the necessary discipline to buy when stocks are out of favor, while carefully avoiding disrupted sectors or companies with negative growth, to enhance your long-term investment success.

This guide decodes how to move beyond market hype to evaluate spin-offs using a structured framework, covering key aspects like 'Sum of the Parts' (SOTP) valuation, managing post-listing volatility, and identifying genuine value creation versus market narrative. Whether you are an aspiring value investor or looking to refine your portfolio strategy, learn how to apply a disciplined seven-point scorecard to assess business fundamentals, capital allocation, and management alignment in upcoming demerger opportunities.

The story looks exciting: gold mining, global project exposure, listed pure-play status, and future production potential. But the financials tell a very different story. Over the last decade, the company has generated very low revenue, reported cumulative losses, and had mostly negative cash flows.

snippet.title: Why PEG Ratio Matters More Than P/E for Stock Valuation?
snippet.description:
Many beginner investors love low PE stocks because they look cheap. But PE ratio has one major limitation — it does not factor in future growth.

That is why a 9x PE stock may deliver poor returns if growth is weak, while a 50x PE stock can still become a multi-bagger if earnings growth is strong.

In this video, we explain the PEG Ratio, how it connects valuation with growth, and why investors should look beyond just PE before judging whether a stock is cheap or expensive.

localized.description:
Why do two companies with the same profit trade at completely different valuations?

Because PE is not just Price-to-Earnings — it is also Perception-to-Earnings. A company’s PE depends on how investors see its future growth potential.

In this video, we explain why a low PE stock is not always cheap, why a high PE stock is not always overvalued, and how growth, sector quality, and cyclicality impact valuations.

This simple guide will help you understand corporate bonds, government bond yields, credit risk, liquidity risk, post-tax returns, and the key factors every bond investor should track before investing. snippet.title: The checklist to follow for right investing ft Helios Mutual Fund
snippet.description:
In this video, we explain a practical 8-filter stock selection framework to identify companies with long-term growth potential, strong quality checks, and reasonable valuations. The first three filters focus on industry factors like industry theme, industry dynamics, and disruption, helping investors understand whether the business has multiple long-term tailwinds. The next three filters evaluate quality of management, corporate governance, and accounting standards, which are critical for building confidence in the company. Finally, the last two filters focus on valuation to ensure the stock is not only high-quality and growth-oriented but also available at a reasonable price. Among all factors, quality of management remains the most important, because even a cheap stock can stay cheap if the management is poor.

snippet.title: One Smart Strategy: Nifty-Like Returns, Lower Downside?
snippet.description:
Everyone talks about Nifty 50’s long-term returns, but what if a simple 50% Nifty and 50% Gold portfolio delivered nearly similar CAGR with much lower losses during major market crashes? From 2006 to 2026, Nifty delivered around 10.9% CAGR, Gold around 9.8%, and a combined portfolio around 10.3%. But during crashes like 2008 and Covid 2020, Gold helped reduce portfolio drawdowns significantly. This video explains the real power of diversification, non-correlated assets, and why surviving drawdowns is just as important as chasing higher returns in long-term wealth creation.

snippet.title: Helios Capital’s Bold Prediction on AI and IT Stocks?
snippet.description:
AI is changing the traditional Indian IT services model, where revenue was largely driven by the number of employees, hours billed, and rate per hour. Earlier, even a regulatory software update for U.S. banks could require large teams working for months. But with AI reducing both manpower and time required, the base of the IT services model may shrink, leading to pressure on revenue growth, margins, and valuations. In this video, we explain why Indian IT companies could face low single-digit growth and margin compression in the AI era.

Watch the complete episode here: https://youtu.be/YuA51_2Uu6I?si=wAgilvys0kSCqyOd

snippet.title: Vedanta to have 4 New Listed Companies from 15th June?
snippet.description:
Vedanta's mega demerger is finally here — from Monday (June 15, 2026), four new companies (Vedanta Aluminium, Vedanta Oil & Gas, Vedanta Power, and Vedanta Iron & Steel) list independently on the stock market, while Vedanta Ltd stays on as the residual metals entity. The same promoter that spent two decades building this conglomerate — acquiring Hindustan Zinc, BALCO, Sesa Goa and Cairn India, then merging everything into Sesa Sterlite in 2013 and Vedanta Ltd in 2015 — is now doing a complete 180, betting that splitting up will unlock "hidden value," kill the conglomerate discount, and give each business its own strategy and valuation. But does a demerger actually create long-term shareholder wealth, or is this a smart financial move to win richer valuations during a bullish commodity cycle? And what about the aggressive dividend payout strategy despite the group's heavy debt load? In this video we break down the full Vedanta demerger story — the history, the logic flip, the value-unlocking thesis, the debt-vs-dividend debate, and what it all means for retail shareholders holding the 1:1 entitlement. Watch till the end for the honest take.

localized.title: How to avoid companies like Rajesh Exports and Gensol?
localized.description:
SEBI’s allegations against Rajesh Exports highlight a crucial investing lesson: big revenue numbers do not always mean strong business performance. snippet.description:
Tata Steel shares slipped over 2% after a major fire broke out at its Port Talbot plant in South Wales, UK. The incident led to temporary evacuation and a precautionary pause at the Hot Rolling Mill, although the company stated that the fire was confined and production is expected to restart soon. With the UK business contributing nearly 10% to Tata Steel’s consolidated revenue, investors are closely tracking the operational impact, damage assessment, and management’s next update.

snippet.title: Small cap investing is evolving - Can momentum and quality make a difference?
snippet.description:
India’s small-cap universe is broad and diverse, offering exposure to emerging businesses across multiple sectors. However, with a large opportunity set also comes the challenge of stock selection.

Factor-based investing aims to address this challenge through a rules-based approach. Momentum factor focuses on companies exhibiting stronger price trends and market participation, while quality factor focuses on businesses with relatively stronger fundamentals.

The Groww Nifty Smallcap 250 Momentum Quality 100 ETF and Groww Nifty Smallcap 250 Momentum Quality 100 Index Fund aim to track the Nifty Smallcap250 Momentum Quality 100 Index (TRI), which selects 100 stocks from the Nifty Smallcap 250 universe based on momentum and quality factors.

NFO closes on: 12 June 2026

Explore ETF: https://www.growwmf.in/mutual-funds/nfo/groww-nifty-smallcap-250-momentum-quality-100-etf

Explore Index Fund: https://www.growwmf.in/mutual-funds/nfo/groww-nifty-smallcap-250-momentum-quality-100-index-fund

The index follows a transparent methodology and provides exposure to a diversified basket of companies selected using momentum and quality characteristics. By combining these factors, it seeks to bring a structured approach to investing within the broader small-cap segment.

If you're looking to explore small-cap investing through a factor-based strategy, these schemes offer exposure to a diversified portfolio of small-cap companies through a single investment.

snippet.title: 80x PE Ratio can be Dangerous for Portfolio Growth?
snippet.description:
In this short, Jiten Parmar from Aurum Capital explains why valuations matter in stock market investing, even for high-quality companies. He highlights how paying very high PE multiples for moderate growth can lead to poor returns or long periods of time correction.

Through examples like Hindustan Unilever and past market cycles, this video simplifies the importance of buying good businesses at reasonable valuations. It also explains why investors should understand PE ratio, earnings growth, market cycles, compounders, and cyclicals before making long-term investment decisions.

Watch this video to learn how valuation discipline can help investors avoid overpaying and improve long-term investing outcomes.

Full Episode: https://youtu.be/QwzqskrQ4f0?si=iUQQgKp6UNbrf_JK

snippet.title: Why did India ban sugar exports?
snippet.description:
Why did India ban sugar exports?

India has banned sugar exports until September 30, 2026 — but what’s the real reason behind this big move? In this video, we break down why the government took this decision, how lower sugar production, rising ethanol demand, and El Niño risks are impacting supply, and what it means for sugar stocks like Balrampur Chini, Triveni Engineering, and Shree Renuka Sugars.

We also explain how this export ban could affect global sugar prices and why international markets are reacting. If you're an investor or tracking commodity trends, this update is crucial.

snippet.title: Helios Capital's Multibagger Strategy Using Elimination Investing
snippet.description:
In this insightful conversation with Dinshaw S Irani, CEO, Helios Capital India, we explore the art of elimination investing, avoiding wealth destroyers, staying disciplined during market euphoria, and building a long-term framework for beating the index.

The discussion covers key lessons from Dinshaw’s decades in the market, how to evaluate management commentary, why diversification matters, how to think about disrupted sectors, and what retail investors can learn from macro risks, commodities, and New-Age companies.

Whether you are a DIY investor, long-term equity investor, or someone trying to build a stronger investing process, this episode offers practical lessons on risk, discipline, valuation, and patience.

snippet.title: 3 stocks with rising profits but cash flow concerns
snippet.description:
3 stocks with rising profits but cash flow concerns

Profit growth doesn’t always mean strong cash flow—discover the crucial secrets Indian investors often miss!
In this video, we analyse Kaynes Technology, Manorama Industries, and Krishana Phoschem—three companies with 40%+ profit growth, and one with a staggering 95% profit jump in just a few years. But beneath impressive financial headlines lurk serious operating cash flow problems, driven by stretched receivables, inventory buildup, and delayed payments. Using fresh data from annual reports and market screeners, you’ll learn why monitoring cash conversion and the working capital cycle is just as important as looking at profits, especially in the fast-evolving Indian stock market.  
Whether you’re an investor or a finance enthusiast, equip yourself with the right analytical tools and mindset to spot hidden risks and make smarter decisions.

snippet.title: Cyclicals vs Compounders: When to Switch & How to Time the Cycle for multibagger returns
snippet.description:
In this insightful conversation, Anupam Gupta sits down with Niteen Dharmawat and Jiten Parmar of Aurum Capital to break down the art and science of cyclical investing.

They dive deep into why cyclicals can outperform compounders at the right time, how to identify cycle bottoms and peaks, and what retail investors often misunderstand about P/E ratios, operating leverage, and value traps. The discussion goes beyond theory into practical frameworks—covering sector selection, capital allocation, concall signals, and exit discipline.

If you’ve ever wondered how seasoned investors navigate sectors like metals, cement, sugar, or banking cycles—this conversation offers a clear, experience-backed perspective.

This episode is especially useful for investors looking to improve their timing, conviction, and risk management in cyclical plays.

The discussion goes beyond theory into practical frameworks—covering sector selection, capital allocation, concall signals, and exit discipline.

If you’ve ever wondered how seasoned investors navigate sectors like metals, cement, sugar, or banking cycles—this conversation offers a clear, experience-backed perspective.

This episode is especially useful for investors looking to improve their timing, conviction, and risk management in cyclical plays.

snippet.title: Leading Fund manager explains his growth investing strategy for Multibagger stocks
snippet.description:
In this episode of Market Ki Baat, we speak with Prabhakar Kudva, co-founder, Samvitti Capital, about how smart investors think about markets, earnings, business cycles, and portfolio construction. From deep value vs high growth to market perception vs fundamental reality, the conversation covers practical frameworks that can help investors make better decisions.

We also discuss the TRAPP framework, how to identify a sector’s growth stage, decode earnings surprises, and read the hidden signals in management commentary. Towards the end, we talk about finding top ideas during earnings season, how young investors can build market sense, quant vs qualitative edge, and how strategy changes as AUM grows. Overall, this episode is packed with practical insights for both new and experienced investors.

snippet.title: Which Gold Loan option is right for you in 2026?
snippet.description:
Which Gold Loan option is right for you in 2026?

Planning to take a gold loan? This video explains the difference between Gold Loan with EMI and Gold Overdraft (OD) in simple terms.

In a Gold Loan EMI, you receive a lump sum amount and pay fixed EMIs with interest on the full loan amount from day one.
In a Gold OD (Overdraft), you get a credit limit and pay interest only on the amount you actually use—making it a more flexible option.

We also cover:
✔ Interest rates comparison
✔ Processing time & documentation
✔ Impact on credit score
✔ Which option is best for business, emergencies, or fixed expenses

Whether you need funds for wedding, business, or emergency, this guide will help you choose the best gold loan option in India and save money on interest.

snippet.title: Why are bonds not always safe?
snippet.description:
Why are bonds not always safe?

Are bonds really safe investments? Many investors believe fixed income and AAA-rated bonds guarantee security—but the reality can be very different. From DHFL’s sudden downgrade to Yes Bank AT1 bond losses, even “safe” bonds can carry serious risks.

In this video, we break down the hidden risks of bond investing including credit risk, liquidity risk, and interest rate risk. Learn what to check before investing in corporate bonds or NBFC bonds in India.

Don’t assume safety just because of ratings or fixed returns, understand the risks before you invest.

snippet.title: Avoid Income Tax Trouble When Buying Dubai Property
snippet.description:
Buying Dubai property with credit cards can lead to serious legal and tax troubles for NRIs. In this video, you will learn why credit card payments for overseas property are flagged by Indian authorities and how this can trigger notices from the Income Tax Department and Enforcement Directorate. Discover the correct legal way to invest in Dubai real estate using RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), how to file the proper documentation, and ways to avoid heavy penalties and TCS tax issues. Whether you're considering your first overseas home or expanding your property portfolio, this comprehensive guide equips you with the essential knowledge to invest safely and hassle-free. Make sure you follow the right process to keep your investments secure and compliant.

In this video, we explain what to check before buying an auction property, including legal verification, due diligence, possession status (physical vs symbolic), pending dues, and risks like multiple loans or ongoing cases.

Learn why bank auction properties are sold “as-is, where-is” and how limited disclosures can impact your investment. We also break down key checks like CIBIL, MCA, NCLT, and DRT in simple terms so you can make a smart decision.

Single vs Joint Home Loan: What’s Better?

Looking to maximize your home loan amount? Discover how applying jointly with a co-applicant can increase your home loan limit from ₹42 lakhs to ₹70 lakhs, unlock tax benefits, and even get an interest rate concession. In this video, you’ll learn why a second income on your home loan application can dramatically improve your borrowing capacity, save you money on interest, and offer greater tax deductions under the old and new tax regimes. Don’t miss the potential pitfalls like credit score impact if EMIs are missed. Watch now and see why two incomes are always better than one for your home loan journey.

snippet.title: Why aren’t Gold & Silver rising during War?
snippet.description:
Why aren’t Gold & Silver rising during War?


When global markets turn tense, Gold is supposed to shine… right? ✨

But this time, even with US–Iran tensions escalating,
Gold and Silver didn’t rally the way everyone expected. 📉

Gold slipped from around 1.69 lakh to nearly 1.60 lakh,
Silver cooled off from 2.9 lakh to 2.7 lakh.

So what’s really happening? 🤔

This isn’t just about war headlines. It’s about liquidity, leverage, and how margin pressure forces even “safe haven” assets to fall.

Sometimes, in the first phase of fear - everything falls together.

So is this just a temporary leverage flush? Or is the Gold rally over?

Comment your view below 👇

snippet.title: Tariffs reduced to 18%, 10 stocks to benefit | India-US Trade Deal 2026
snippet.description:
India and the United States have announced a major trade agreement that significantly reduces tariffs on Indian goods, improving India’s competitiveness in the US market. In this video, we explain the key terms of the deal, why the tariff cut from 50% to 18% matters, and how it positions India relative to other Asian exporters. We then analyze the potential sector-wise impact across textiles, chemicals, auto ancillaries, consumer exports, seafood, gems & jewellery, and solar manufacturing. The video highlights companies with meaningful US exposure, discusses export trends, margin implications, and outlines key risks, including policy uncertainty and near-term volatility. snippet.title: Stocks to benefit from India EU trade deal
snippet.description:
India and the European Union have signed a Free Trade Agreement, marking a significant step in strengthening bilateral trade. In this video, we explain the agreement in simple terms and analyze which sectors could benefit the most and where challenges may emerge.

We look at potential upside for textiles & apparel, pharmaceuticals, and chemicals due to tariff reductions, better market access, and shifting global supply chains. We also discuss other possible beneficiaries such as leather, seafood, and jewellery. On the flip side, we examine sectors like passenger automobiles and alcoholic beverages, where increased competition from imports could create pressure.

This video is a sector-level analysis aimed at understanding the broader impact of the India–EU FTA on Indian companies and trade dynamics.

Copper is quietly emerging as one of the most important strategic metals of this decade. From AI data centers and electric vehicles to renewable energy and power grids, copper demand is rising rapidly - while global supply struggles to keep pace.

In this video, we break down why copper is in focus in 2025, the key demand drivers behind its silent rally, the potential supply-demand mismatch ahead, and most importantly, how Indian investors can participate in the copper story through stocks, MCX futures, metal ETFs, and global exposure options.

This is a data-backed, neutral analysis - not a price prediction - designed to help investors understand probabilities, risks, and opportunities in copper investing.

snippet.title: Is India Entering a New Small Cap Cycle?
snippet.description:
India’s small cap companies have seen significant growth over the last decade — not just in numbers, but in how businesses are built, scaled, and managed.
In this video, we break down:
How the size and scale of India’s small cap companies have evolved over time

The role of capacity, capability, and confidence in supporting business growth

How improvements in infrastructure, digital systems, banking, and governance have strengthened the ecosystem for smaller companies

Why outcomes within the small cap universe vary widely across companies

The importance of deep research and bottom-up stock selection in identifying long-term opportunities

The video also explains the investment approach behind the Groww Small Cap Fund — an open-ended equity scheme that aims to generate long-term capital appreciation by investing predominantly in small cap stocks using a disciplined, bottom-up framework focused on Quality, Growth and Reasonable Price (QGaRP).

snippet.description:
This video breaks the myth of using P/E ratio as a one-size-fits-all valuation tool. 

We explain why different sectors command different P/E multiples, how cyclicality, capital intensity, and earnings quality impact valuations, and why low P/E stocks can often be value traps. 

Using real data, case studies, and investor frameworks, we decode when P/E works, when it misleads, and how smart investors combine it with growth, risk, and business fundamentals to make better decisions.

The Nifty Smallcap 250 has faced a correction over the last year due to slowing earnings growth and high valuations, yet specific stocks are defying this trend by breaking out to all-time highs. In this video, we analyze three such small-cap stocks that are showing strong technical momentum despite the broader market weakness.

Our first pick is a diversified engineering company manufacturing automotive and industrial parts, which is currently undertaking heavy CAPEX and eyeing opportunities in the data center space.

 The second stock is a leading global manufacturer of specialty steel wire ropes that has aggressively reduced its borrowings while serving critical sectors like oil & offshore and mining. 

The final pick is a prominent South Indian cement player recently acquired by an industry giant, now focusing on operational turnaround and green energy expansion.

snippet.title: Highest FII selling, weak Rupee ? What should investors do?
snippet.description:
This video breaks down why Nifty 50 returns look very different for Indian and US investors, even when the index performance is the same.

We explain how currency movement (USD-INR) changes real returns, why rupee depreciation impacts foreign investors, and how RBI’s recent shift to a more market-driven currency regime has increased volatility. Using long-term data, we compare INR vs USD returns, decode FII-DII flow dynamics, and highlight why India remains attractive despite currency headwinds.

The video also covers:

How rupee depreciation affects compounding over time

Why FIIs continue investing in India despite lower USD returns

The growing role of domestic investors in stabilizing markets

How currency can act as a drag or a tailwind depending on the investor

A clear, data-backed perspective on equity returns, currency risk, and global investing.
